title: Equipment: router, switch, hub, modem, access point, firewall and load balancer

videos.script: Walk into a shop that sells network equipment and most of it looks the same. A metal case, a row of ports, some lights. {{shelf}} The label is no help either. The box your provider put on the shelf at home is sold as a router, and it is four devices in one case. So this lesson names each device by what it reads. {{layers}} A switch reads hardware addresses and learns where each one lives. A hub reads nothing and repeats everything. A router reads IP addresses and moves packets between networks. A firewall reads ports and connections, and decides what passes. {{lab}} You will watch each one work in a lab. It is an office with four computers on a switch, a router that is also the firewall, a provider, and a load balancer in front of two web servers. {{switch}} You will see the switch keep a conversation away from a third computer. Then the same switch, made to behave like a hub, hands that computer every frame. {{firewall}} You will watch the firewall count the packets it refuses, and the load balancer send requests to two servers in turn. {{modem}} The modem and the access point need a phone line and a radio. The lab has neither, so those two are described, not run.
